screens.title: Settings
screens.purpose: Reach controls and service functions without crowding the musical HOME.
screens.select: Choose Harmony, Controls, Display, MIDI/USB, Sound, or Tools/System
screens.exit: HOME → Progressions; GLO → previous musical workspace
states: Returning retains selected row
No settings write/transport change just from opening
playerSteps: Press GLO.
Turn SELECT to choose a group.
Press SEL to open it.

screens.title: Harmony
screens.purpose: Control live root-key chord assistance only; explicit Progression PLAY and fixed-note recordings retain their own content.
screens.select: No item to select
states: Off leaves normal playing alone
On + Quantize Off or non-seven-note scale: Auto?; explain fallback
On/Off clears selected modifiers/inversion history but preserves held roots/HOLD
No Rich/Dreamy/Custom styles
Explicit Progression PLAY plays arranged full chords with live Harmony Off; it does not switch global Harmony On or collapse the plan to single notes
A recorded Take/Song plays its fixed notes regardless of live Harmony
Unsupported-Auto single-note fallback applies to live root assistance, not arranged Progression playback
playerSteps: Use K1 On/Off for live root-key assistance.
With On, play roots and choose colors with modifier buttons.
PLAY hears arranged Progression chords even when live Harmony is Off.

screens.title: Controls
screens.purpose: Group musical performance rules and deliberate button assignments.
screens.select: Choose page
states: Top Lock is the supported primary layout
Legacy layouts are import/compatibility concerns, not a new HOME mode selector
playerSteps: Choose Play behavior or an assignment editor with SELECT, then press SEL.

screens.title: Play behavior
screens.purpose: Control touch and chord movement without restoring global harmony styles.
screens.select: Change page: Play behavior / Quantize and glide
states: Retrigger choices: Wait, Notes, Slide, Chord; guide must describe exact audible differences
No new global harmony style
playerSteps: Use K1–K4 to change the visible values.
Use SELECT for Quantize and glide.

screens.title: Quantize and glide
screens.purpose: Move Glide off HOME while keeping key/scale setup understandable.
screens.select: Change page: Play behavior / Quantize and glide
states: Off / Basic / Full
Quantize Off: key/scale editing disabled with a direct route to this setting
Browsing an idea can restore Basic as specified by the progression workflow
Unsupported Auto: single-note fallback; never falsely label a full automatic chord
playerSteps: Choose Basic or Full for Auto.
Turn K2 for the chord sound's Glide.
Return HOME for direct Rhythm/Key/Scale/Tempo controls.

screens.title: Modifier assignments
screens.purpose: Assign an upper modifier slot without competing with Chord Lab's SEL destination.
screens.select: Choose an assignable upper button
screens.algorithm: No tabs; HOME ALGORITHM scene cycle is not active here
states: Choices: None, 6, 7, 9, Add9, 11, 13, Sus2, Sus4, Add2, Add4, Major, Minor, Dim, Aug, Power
Inversion: Root / Smooth / 1st / 2nd / 3rd
Bass selects an available chord tone; display the resolved note
HOLD slot is read-only: HOLD is not a modifier
Conflicting selections show ! and actual applied modifiers remain clear
Harmony Off: assignments retained; Manual forms remain separate
playerSteps: Choose the slot with SELECT.
Turn K1 for the modifier, K3 for inversion and K4 for bass tone.
Play notes to hear the result; selecting a slot does not itself change the playing root.

screens.title: Manual chord forms
screens.purpose: Preserve user chord forms for Harmony Off and imported content under an advanced route.
screens.select: Choose a form button
states: HOLD/Off slot read-only
Harmony On: explain these are retained manual forms; do not silently switch Harmony
Type/Add/Inversion/Bass ranges follow the active form model
playerSteps: Choose a form button.
Use K1–K4 for the visible form choices.
Turn Harmony Off explicitly to use manual forms.

screens.title: Appearance · Character
screens.purpose: Choose Devil/Ember or Cat/Plum; the entire palette is tied to the character.
screens.select: Choose another system page
states: The approved soft mascot reference supersedes Instrument/Studio/Editorial for this build. Exactly Devil/Ember and Cat/Plum are selectable.
Character selection changes the entire palette, not music, transport, source or sounds. There is no independent theme or accent control.
Motion On follows real output/activity and shared musical phase. Off settles every effect; actual values and transport remain truthful.
Preference v5 preserves the 44-byte record and migrates v1–v4 favorites, Motion and Click without a load-time write.
playerSteps: Open GLO → Display and turn K1 CHARACTER to Devil or Cat.
The palette follows the character throughout HOME, menus and startup.
K4 selects Motion On or Off; return HOME to play.

screens.title: Motion
screens.purpose: Choose adaptive On or totally Off, with no additional motion-style, intensity or speed selector.
screens.select: Choose another system page
states: Exactly two user options: On / Off. No Quiet, Expressive, Reduced, Calm, Intensity or Speed motion preference.
On derives a bounded response from smoothed volume/output level and active instrument-part count. Smooth level/activity changes so short percussion transients do not abruptly change the response.

Use the shared clock and resolved playing/ownership. The firmware uses a real post-MASTER activity snapshot; physical tuning remains pending. Prototype loudness/layers sliders are not device controls.
The demonstration’s up-to-eight layer count is not a promise of eight hardware instrument parts, engines, tracks or voices.

Retain functional beat/playhead, chord transition, parameter/bank/focus, REC and confirmed Saved feedback across all nine studies, including Morph/Bloom visual motion. Unsupported musical features remain explicitly studies.

Off stops every animation and transition, including CSS pulses/halos, fades/interpolation, focus/parameter/bank, Morph/Bloom and Saved responses. Chord/notes/degree/cursor/status update immediately to the correct settled state.
OS reduced motion may privately force effective Off; it must not create a third Reduced user option.

Tune the hidden adaptive curve through engineering and physical validation, not a manual Motion Intensity/Speed dial. Measure and cap cadence, dirty regions, pixel work, scratch memory and foreground latency with demanding sound/drums/USB; no browser FPS/CPU/polyphony promises.
playerSteps: Open GLO → Display.
Turn K4 for Motion On or Off.
Return HOME; musical and saved-data state remains live.

screens.title: Secondary scenes
screens.purpose: Historical exploration; not a route or appearance option in the two-character build.
screens.select: Choose Accent / Motion / Legacy scenes
states: Not implemented in this build; character and palette are coupled.
playerSteps: Use GLO → Display → K1 CHARACTER for the implemented appearance choices.

screens.title: MIDI
screens.purpose: Preserve MIDI note routing and external synchronization without hiding it in a technical dashboard.
screens.select: Choose MIDI / Channels / USB capture
states: Clock Internal / Receive / Send maps active Off / In / Out
Notes input: FM-1 keys / Roots / Direct
Direct disables generic input channel; its part channels apply instead
Changing input interpretation/channel releases owned incoming notes
MIDI Out Off also disables clock-send output; make this visible
playerSteps: Set Notes in and the input channel for an external keyboard.
Choose Receive for an external MIDI clock.
Use SELECT for the part channels or USB capture status.

screens.title: MIDI channels
screens.purpose: Show part routing explicitly, including compatibility-only Layer where retained.
screens.select: Choose MIDI / Channels / USB capture
states: 1–16 per available part
Layer is labelled Legacy or unavailable after retirement
Overlapping channels are allowed deliberately; explain Direct input ambiguity if applicable
Channel changes release previous routing's owned notes
playerSteps: Set the destination channel for each part.
In Direct input mode, use the relevant part channel on the sending device.

screens.title: Waiting for clock
screens.purpose: Explain armed external synchronization instead of showing a misleading editable local tempo.
screens.entry: SYS-MIDI Clock Receive; no pulses received
screens.select: No action

buttons.PLAY: Arm/stop locally; wait for explicit external Start/Continue

screens.exit: GLO → SYS-MIDI; HOME → externally armed Progressions
states: Planned successor policy: Receive without pulses is Waiting/armed; local tempo stays EXT and is not editable
External Start begins the phrase; Continue resumes the kept position; external Stop stops accompaniment
Pulses alone after loss do not restart playback
This is a successor design decision, not a claim about current firmware
playerSteps: Set Clock to Receive.
Start the master transport when ready.
Use the master device's Start or Continue command; clock pulses alone do not restart a stopped phrase.

screens.title: Clock lost
screens.purpose: Stop accompaniment safely on lost external clock, keep position, and preserve independent live HOLD.
screens.select: No action

buttons.HOME: Return to Progressions with Clock lost visible
buttons.GLO: Back to MIDI; choose Internal deliberately
buttons.PLAY: Keep accompaniment stopped/armed; do not bypass external source silently

screens.exit: GLO → SYS-MIDI; HOME → Progressions with clock warning
states: Stops/releases accompaniment-owned notes only; independent live HOLD remains
Retains the last phrase position for external Continue
Clock pulses alone do not restart; external Start/Continue or choosing Internal is required
Planned timeout: two last-estimated quarter-note periods, clamped 500–4000 ms; validate on device before release
Player guide omits numeric timeout; current firmware's old roughly-300 ms lock detector is not this successor policy
playerSteps: Check the external clock source.
Send Start to restart or Continue to resume its kept position.
Choose Internal explicitly to regain local tempo control; then use PLAY deliberately.

screens.title: USB capture
screens.purpose: Show the actual host-selected audio stream and routing; avoid an invented on-device rate switch.
screens.select: Choose MIDI / Channels / USB capture
states: Disconnected / connected-closed / capturing 44.1 / capturing 48 / suspended / reconnecting
Safe Mode: MIDI + console, audio capture unavailable
Computer-to-FM-1 audio playback is not provided
Capture channels retain documented master/stem level and FX behavior
No new sample-rate or recording toggle is implied by this page
playerSteps: Connect a USB data cable.
Choose the FM-1 input and rate in the recording app.
Record inputs 1/2 for the whole mix; select stems deliberately.

screens.title: Sound
screens.purpose: Keep sound selection and advanced editing available behind the writing workflow.

fields.label: Options
fields.value: Choose sound · Envelope · Advanced · Save sound

screens.select: Highlight Presets / Envelope / Advanced sound / Sound actions; SEL enters the canonical route

buttons.ENV: Open ENV_ENVELOPE with named normal target; legacy Layer has an explicit compatibility route

states: Target Chord / Bass; Layer only via compatibility route
Explicit target is shown on every sound page
Bank filter affects sound browsing only; never the progression list
No matching sound in a bank: say Empty bank and allow All
Preview edits are not represented as saved until persistence succeeds
PRESETS globally changes chord sound; K2 or SOUND_PRESETS SELECT explicitly chooses the named target sound
playerSteps: Open GLO → Sound.
Choose Presets, Envelope, Advanced sound or Sound actions with SELECT then SEL.
Use explicit Chord/Bass target controls; PRESETS always changes the chord sound.

screens.title: Advanced sound
screens.purpose: Group the retained engine's deep pages without taking note keys away for navigation.
screens.select: Choose a named engine section; SEL enters its first/last page
screens.algorithm: Shortcut: choose OP1–OP6 / Pitch / Global for FM6; corresponding VA section for VA
states: FM6 and VA retain their real current editor pages
No deep editor: clear Not available for this engine
Changing target/engine retargets safely and names it; no stale wrong-part edits
Note keys remain performance keys in the successor design
playerSteps: Open Sound → Advanced.
Choose the named section with SELECT then SEL; ALGORITHM is a section shortcut.
Inside a parameter page, SELECT chooses its page, ALGORITHM chooses section, and K1–K4 edit the visible values.
